intuition.title: Three material protocols, separate assay contexts
intuition.text: The main supplies aqueous GSH-capped CdTe synthesis, citrate reduction of gold and subsequent peptide modification of the gold colloid. The mixed Au-Ps/CdTe optical assays are nonconjugated probe mixtures, not a new Au–CdTe composite synthesis. Supporting assay series retain their own aliquots, concentrations and unknown specimen links.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Scheme 1 and Materials and Methods

intuition.title: CdTe morphology remains missing
intuition.text: The main gives NaBH4/Te precursor preparation, CdCl2–GSH stock, pH 9.0, 400 µL/0.8 µL aliquots and 100 °C for 30 min. It directs TEM characterization to Figure S1, which lies in excluded SI. The 520 nm fluorescence maximum and estimated particle concentration do not establish a CdTe diameter, shape or crystal phase.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Synthesis of CdTe QDs and Figure 1b

intuition.title: Gold TEM belongs to peptide-modified gold
intuition.text: Citrate-stabilized gold is prepared by adding 1.6 mL of 1% citrate to 50 mL of 0.25 mM HAuCl4 at boiling, followed by 10 min at boiling and 4 °C storage. Main Figure 4B and the about-18 nm average explicitly concern Au-Ps after peptide modification. Figure 4C shows enzyme-induced aggregation without a named caspase dose. Neither panel is a CdTe micrograph.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–4, Au synthesis, Results and Figure 4B–C

intuition.title: Thiol-peptide modification is source-reported
intuition.text: The peptide stock is 2 mM DK (Mpa)-12 in phosphate buffer at pH 7.4. AuNPs and peptide are mixed at a nominal 1:150 molar ratio, stirred for 10 h at room temperature, centrifuged and redispersed. The authors interpret the FTIR and gel changes as peptide attachment through Au–S bonding; no surface coverage or atomistic conformation is measured.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Modification of AuNPs and Figure 2

intuition.title: Cleavage and inner-filter interpretation
intuition.text: The authors propose removal of the negatively charged DDDEVD segment by caspase-3, leaving GRRRR-Mpa on gold and promoting electrostatic aggregation. They attribute fluorescence recovery to reduced spectral overlap as gold absorption shifts from 520 to 680 nm. This mechanism is their interpretation. Main statements of negative zeta potential refer to excluded Figure S3; no zeta magnitudes are supplied here.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Scheme 1, mechanism and IFE discussion

intuition.title: Keep concentration and ratio discrepancies visible
intuition.text: Figure 3 lists Au-Ps concentrations on a 10−9 M scale and CdTe at 1.14 × 10−8 M, but its nominal Au-Ps:CdTe ratio list behaves as though the concentrations were comparable. The fluorescent-assay Methods also say 1:1, while Figure 5 labels about a tenfold concentration difference. No exponent, ratio, dilution or aliquot is silently repaired.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–4, Assay Methods and Figures 3–5

intuition.title: Assay properties are not synthesis outputs
intuition.text: The main reports a 27.68–129.15 pM linear range and an 18 pM detection limit. Figure 5C annotates Y = 0.0039X + 1.0376 and R² = 0.9967. These describe the fluorescent assay, not particle morphology or separate materials syntheses. Bars and curve points are not digitized.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4–5, Figure 5 and Conclusions

intuition.title: Unreviewed sources stay outside this contribution
intuition.text: All 38 main bibliography entries are retained as citations. Figures S1–S6 and their numerical contents are excluded; their main-text mentions do not establish that the supplement was read. Prior-method and extinction-coefficient citations are not new inspected source documents.

general_background.title: Formation from dissolved precursors
general_background.summary: When dissolved species become supersaturated with respect to a solid, nucleation and growth can compete with continued precursor conversion. Mixing, complexation and solution chemistry can change that balance.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
